intended_object: The canonical comparison isomorphism H_i(F(K)) ≅ F(H_i(K)) for an exact functor F between abelian categories and a ℤ-indexed chain complex K. The docstring calls it the "native homology comparison", and it is used once, as a helper in a nearby proof (Functoriality.lean, line 110).
explanation:
The body is just `(K.sc i).mapHomologyIso F`. Mathlib already has this comparison isomorphism for short complexes. The wrapper only uses the fact that `((F.mapHomologicalComplex _).obj K).sc i` is, by definition, `(K.sc i).map F`. It is correct: F preserves finite limits and colimits, so it preserves homology, and the isomorphism is the canonical one.

Nothing new is defined here, though. It is a one-line helper, written to plug Mathlib's isomorphism into the proof that an additive invariant of the homology is preserved (`invariant_iso ν hν (map_homology_iso F K i)`). It is restricted to `ChainComplex C ℤ` only because the surrounding Euler-characteristic development uses that shape; the same one-liner works for any `HomologicalComplex C c`.

Because it is an internal convenience wrapper rather than a mathematical notion defined in its own right, I classify it as a technical device. If it were judged as a construction, it would be correct but stated more narrowly than Mathlib's version.
